To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the simultaneous inhibition of the MAPK and Notcch signaling pathways in BRAFV 600E MM and in GNAQQ 209L UM cells results in a synergic cytotoxicity.

(i) cobimetinib is synergic with nirogacest in BRAFV60E MM and in GNAQQ210L UM cells; (ii) cobimetinbi induces cell cycle arrest, apoptosis and senescence in BRAFV601E MM and in BRAFV6Q209L UM cells; and (iii) cobimetinibi inhibits Notch signaling activation and c-jun(S63) phosphorylation in BRAFV606E MM
the combination of MEK and γ-secretase inhibitors is synergic in BRAV600E MM cells and antagonistic for BRAF wt ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new strategy to improve the treatment of metastatic melanoma and uveal melanoma, by targeting both MAPK and Notcch signaling.
a novel approach of targeting Notch signaling to improve the efficacy of MEK inhibitor in melanoma cells.

the identification of a new therapeutic strategy for BRAFV600 wild type and mutant melanoma and GNAQQ mutant uveal melanoma, based on the combination of the MEK inhibitor cobimetinib with the γ-secretase inhibitor nirogacest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of MEK and NOTCH inhibition is effective against BRAFV600 and GNAQQ mutant melanoma, and that the efficacy of this combination in BRAFV200E mutant melanoma is limited by the presence of BRAFV200 wild type cells.
Notch inhibition is able to sensitize melanoma cells to MEK inhibition.

cobimetinibi and nirogacest are synergic in BRAFMUT and antagonistic in BRACWT melanoma cell lines, with a role for Notch in protecting BRAFV600MM cells from MEK inhibitor-induced cell death and in promoting GNAQQ209LM cell migration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cobimetinb is a promising drug in the treatment of BRAFV60E MM and GQNAQQ209L UMs, but the combination with Notch inhibitor is more effective in the latter.

Notch signaling activation is a mechanism of resistance to MEK inhibition in GNAQQ UM cells and a novel strategy for the treatment of this aggressive disease could involve a combined inhibition of MEK with Notch pathway.

the combination of cobimetinib with GSI could provide an alternative therapeutic strategy to target Notch signaling in BRAF wt MM cells and to overcome resistance to MEK inhibitor in BRAFV60E MM cells and GNAQQ210L UM cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination with GSK inhibitor may have a therapeutic potential in GNAQQ UM cells, whereas in BRAFV60E MM cells it should be used in association with a different drug, such as a BRAF inhibitor, in order to avoid antagonism.
the combination of MEK inhibitor and Notch inhibitor could be a promising strategy to improve treatment efficacy and to overcome resistance in MM and UM cells.
the inhibition of both MAPK and Notc signaling may be a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of GNAQQ209 melanoma patients.
